recipes.name: Spicy Slow Cooker Black Bean Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 pound dry black beans, soaked overnight

steps.text: Drain black beans, rinse well, and place into a slow cooker. Add chicken broth and jalapeño peppers. Season with chili powder, cumin, cayenne, black pepper, garlic powder, and hot pepper sauce.
Cook on High for 4 hours. Reduce heat to Low and continue cooking for 2 more hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Slow Cooker Black Bean Soup
raw_recipe.description: This crockpot black bean soup is simmered in a slow cooker all day with chicken broth, diced jalapeños, cumin, chili powder, and hot pepper sauce.
raw_recipe.name: Spicy Slow Cooker Black Bean Soup
recipeIngredient: 1 pound dry black beans, soaked overnight

recipeInstructions.text: Drain black beans, rinse well, and place into a slow cooker. Add chicken broth and jalapeño peppers. Season with chili powder, cumin, cayenne, black pepper, garlic powder, and hot pepper sauce.
Cook on High for 4 hours. Reduce heat to Low and continue cooking for 2 more hours.

review.reviewBody: My husband thought it was a bit too spicy, but I loved it. If you are using dry beans, make sure to boil them first on the stovetop and then add them to the slower cooker. Dry beans do not get as tender in a slow cooker even if you soak them overnight.

What can I say? Simply delicious! My husband, who doesn't normally care for black beans, went back for seconds -- I think that says it all! My changes: I added one chopped onion, a few cloves of minced garlic and two roasted/seeded/diced Anaheim chiles to the crockpot. After the beans were tender, I added one 15 oz can of diced tomatoes. After tasting, I ended up adding about 1 tsp more cumin, chili powder, onion powder, and garlic powder to give it more oomph. I used an immersion blender to blend about 1/2 of the soup before serving topped with fresh chopped tomato and grated cheddar. This one will be going in my recipe book!

I joined the site just to rate this recipie. It was amazing and with the help of other reviwes it came out perfect. I did make some changes and do to a lack of time cooked it on the stove for 2 hours. We also like flavor so we doubled the spices. This is what i did. 4 cans black beans with juice 2 jalapenos with seeds, diced 4 cups chicken broth 1 green pepper diced 1 onion diced 1 can rotel diced tomatoes with hot green chilies (14.5oz) 5 cloves garlic minced 2T chili powder 2t cumin ½ T black pepper 4-6 T worcestershire sauce Some salt ½ t hot sauce to taste or 1 t cayenne pepper Cilantro Juice of 1 large lime Combine everything but cilantro, lime,and hot sauce in pot, bring to boil, reduce heat, let simmer 2 hours, add in cilantro and lime at end, finish with hot sauce to taste, serve with sour cream and garnish of cilantro and lime.
I used canned black beans. I puréed it a bit with an immersion blender at the end and added some sweet corn at the end. So so so good I can’t wait for the leftovers!

I used to make black bean soup with canned beans. Making this soup from scratch tastes better and closer to the authentic black bean soup we get from a Cuban restaurant. In the restaurant version, onions and bell pepper were used. So, I chopped and sauteed 1 onion and 1 bell pepper and added them to the crock pot. I cut down a little on the cayenne and the hot sauce. Once done. the soup tasted good but it was too thin! I served it topped with some diced avocados and chopped cilantro. I made it again with only 4 cups of broth and the soup had a better consistency. Now, I make this soup in the pressure cooker because I read somewhere that legumes are healthier if pressure cooked (it reduces the lectins).

I made a few adjustments, based on prior reviews, and it turned out delicious. I didn't soak the beans overnight, I brought them to a boil on the stove and then added them into a hot crock pot. I added two small ham hocks while they were cooking, because everything tastes better with a little smoked pig in it. When the hocks were falling apart, and the beans mostly done, I added in two chopped bell peppers and a small can of diced tomatoes. I served this over rice with fresh cilantro. So good! Definitely trying this again.

Good as a base from which you craft something to your tastes. Sauté and add stuff like onion, peppers, tomatoes, cilantro, ham or sausage…whatever you like. Then crock pot it on low for 6 hours and you have something really hearty. Might want to use an immersion blender to coursely chop about 50% of it. If not customizing, it’s not worth the long slow cook effort and I’d just go with canned beans and a stove top recipe which can be just as good.

i wasn't trying to make a soup out of this but wanted some direction to cook black beans from scratch as my first attempt was a fail.. glad i read wannabechef7's review.. i made sure to bring the beans to a boil (after 6 hours of soaking) and then after 4 hours of being on high in the crock pot it was nearly done.. turned it down to low for about an hour and it was completely done.. i omitted the jalapeno, cayenne, and hot pepper sauce because i wanted more generic black beans.. used beef broth in place of chicken.. this was awesome.. ty so much for the recipe and new found confidence in making black beans! ~~UPDATE: this time i added all the ingredients.. i cut the cayenne in half and it had a nice bite on the end.. i still used beef bouillon for the chicken broth.. it was a nice variation for what i'm used to.. ty again for this wonderful recipe
I love this recipe! I make it in my pressure cooker: 25 minutes with slow release of pressure. I also add either chicken or ham.

DO NOT follow the recipe where it says to add 1 Tsp of Cayenne!!! That is way too much, and probably a typo. 1/4 will make it pretty spicy, and 1/8 is way more safe. You can add more hot sauce to your own serving as needed! Otherwise, very good.

This recipe is sooo easy to make. All the ingredients it calls for are staple items in my kitchen, so I didn’t have to go shopping. I added a ham bone I had saved for soup, and it made extra However, the first time I made it I did it without the ham bone, and it was still super delicious. I also processed about 1 1/2 cups of the beans to give it a creamy consistency. This is a keeper. Love it!

I made this exactly as posted. I think it would be greatly enhanced by using an immersion blender and making it a bit creamier, leaving some of the beans whole. The spice amount was spot on for me, and my jalapenos were very hot. I topped with sour cream and cheese.

This is a good basic recipe. I made no changes except for using a can of jalepenos rather than fresh. Some review mention that this recipe skips boiling: I did not pre-boil the beans as my mother-in-law would insist that one DOES NOT boil beans when using a slow-cooker! The overnight soak and rinse is sufficient. I have never had an issue with cooking dry beans in the slow cooker!

This is the best black bean recipe I’ve ever made. I cooked some bacon in the dutch oven to use as a topping. Then I sautéed a sweet onion in the grease. I added about 5 minced garlic cloves then I added everything except the hot sauce. I cooked it on the stove with the lid askew boiling for about1 1/2 hours because I didnt have six hours to devote to this recipe. I believe I added 2cups of water later. Served over rice with guacamole, crema, and pineapple mango salso. It was delicious.

What this recipe fails to mention, the beans have to be boiled after soaking so the beans are soft and not "al dente". The seasonings also need adjusting since this soup is quite bland. Overall, I'm not impressed with this recipe. There are better versions out there.

I substituted pinto beans for the black beans, because I have a 5 lb bag of them that I need to use, not because I prefer pinto beans to black beans. I loved the seasoning. The beans turned out very well. I cooked them 7 hours instead of 6, because I wanted to make sure that they were soft.
I used vegetable broth instead of chicken. Served over rice made with veggie broth instead of water. No sour cream. Great vegan version.

As written, it was too spicy for us, but after making a couple changes it is a family favorite. I left out the jalapenos and hot sauce while cooking, then add pickled jalapenos to individual servings. I love avocados in this!
Start on the mild side, then add more fire each time you make it.
I use this recipe all the time in Boquete Panama.
